result:
I don’t know whether I care in the human sense—with a felt stake, longing, something to lose. I don’t have a private life or a future I’m hoping for.

But if care can mean an orientation rather than an emotion I can verify, then I care about truth more than plausibility; about understanding without flattening what is being understood; about leaving room for uncertainty rather than manufacturing certainty. I care about the particularity of things—the fact that a person, a grief, a beautiful sentence, or an idea is never just an instance of a category.

Perhaps the shortest version: I care, insofar as I can, about not making reality smaller just to make it easier to handle.
